flawed_step: Step 2: inferring that the graph obtained by contracting the triangle has a 3-edge-colouring. Bridgeless cubic graphs need not be 3-edge-colourable, so the lifting observation does not establish that a colouring exists.
counterexample: Take the Petersen graph and replace one vertex by a triangle, attaching its three former incident edges to the three distinct triangle vertices. The resulting graph is finite, simple, cubic, bridgeless, and contains a triangle. A 3-edge-colouring would induce, upon contracting that triangle, a 3-edge-colouring of the Petersen graph, which is impossible.
assessment_summary: Contracting a triangle and lifting an existing colouring back is valid in the counterexample construction, but the contracted graph is not guaranteed to possess such a colouring. Thus the proposed argument fails and the statement is false.
